articleHeadline: Unsafe injection practices can lead to HIV outbreaks: NMC
articleSummary: Unsafe injection practices can trigger HIV and other blood-borne infection outbreaks; the National Medical Commission (NMC) issued a nationwide advisory to medical colleges to enforce safe injection practices to prevent HIV, HBV, and HCV transmission. In Srinagar and across India, institutions must ensure full compliance with national infection prevention guidelines, including hand hygiene, sterile single-use needles and syringes, and a strict ban on reusing injection equipment under any circumstances. Sharps and injection-related waste must be segregated and disposed of per Biomedical Waste Management Rules, 2016. The advisory urges gradual adoption of safety-engineered auto-disable syringes and regular training plus competency assessments for healthcare workers. Needle-stick injuries or infection clusters must be promptly reported and investigated. Hospitals should provide post-exposure prophylaxis as per NACO guidelines and conduct ongoing audits through infection control teams. Reuse of equipment, unsafe vial sharing, needle recapping, and improper disposal are non-negotiable safety breaches with zero tolerance.

They arrived at Detroit's McNamara Airport on January 25 from Republic of Congo, where mpox outbreaks occurred. A case contained 113 vials packed inside foam coolers; tests showed deactivated mpox virus, chickenpox virus, and human DNA. The scientists allegedly failed to declare the materials or obtain required permissions. Of 20 vials analyzed, 17 contained deactivated mpox, one contained chickenpox, and two contained human DNA; strain and origin were not clear. Munster reportedly told investigators that documents were on his laptop and that “you don’t need them, I do this all the time.” They face up to five years in prison if convicted; NIH cooperates with authorities. The Congo outbreak caused more than 2,000 deaths and was declared over in April, with clade I noted for higher lethality but the strain here is unspecified.

articleHeadline: Women are the first caregivers in this Ebola outbreak and the most at risk
articleSummary: Eastern Congo's Ebola outbreak in Bunia, one of the fastest-spreading on record, leaves women like Aline Kasiwa as the primary caregivers for ill relatives. She avoids bringing her mother to the hospital where infection could be confirmed, citing reports of many deaths there, including nurses. Three Ebola patients fled treatment centers in Beni after Saturday’s raids. The ADF, a loose network with ties to Islamic State, has intensified attacks on civilians and Congolese forces in the region since 2014. This incident compounds the ongoing 17th Ebola epidemic identified in the DRC since 1976, complicating containment as displacement raises transmission risk. The government condemned the killings and pledged that the fight against the ADF remains a priority, though insecurity undermines response.

articleSummary: On June 4, 2026, Nghệ An Obstetrics and Pediatrics Hospital in Vietnam treated a 23-month-old child with hand-foot-and-mouth disease stage IV complicated by neurological and respiratory failure. The patient initially presented with high fever, irritability, seizures, a vesicular rash on the hands and feet, and oral ulcers. After rapid deterioration with seizures and hypoxemia, the child was transferred to the hospital, where clinicians diagnosed HFMD stage IV with brain and respiratory complications likely linked to Enterovirus 71 (EV71). Intensive management included endotracheal intubation, central venous access, invasive arterial BP monitoring, anti-edema therapy, sedation, intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG), and continuous blood filtration. After several days, the child improved: alert, weaned from ventilation, breathing independently, and eating normally, with no neurological sequelae. Physicians warn that EV71 can cause rapid progression to severe disease; parents should seek care for high fever, startle responses, limb tremors, prolonged crying, lethargy, or rapid breathing.

articleHeadline: Rapid tests for Bundibugyo virus in DR Congo
articleSummary: Bundibugyo virus outbreak in DR Congo has >300 confirmed cases and >40 deaths as of May 31, 2026. Transmission ongoing for weeks with cases in urban centers such as Kampala, Uganda, and Goma, DR Congo, indicating likely numerous undetected transmission chains. Ebola-like fever symptoms complicate screening, as fever and non-specific symptoms overlap malaria and other infections. PCR remains essential for confirmation, but automated PCR throughput is unlikely to meet the screening demand. Rapid antigen tests could expand screening and isolation, yet no rapid test has prospectively validated data for Bundibugyo; existing tests mainly target Ebola virus (Orthoebolavirus zairense) with potential cross-reactivity; data derive from laboratory evaluations, package inserts, or field studies. Tests should be evaluated outbreak-condition side-by-side with RT-PCR on identical samples. If sensitivity is poor, serial testing might help; positive results should trigger isolation pending PCR. Urgent investment is needed to develop and validate Bundibugyo-specific rapid diagnostics, including immunoassays and CRISPR-based SHERLOCK platforms for large-scale deployment.

articleSummary: Bundibugyo Ebola virus disease (BVD) outbreak in the DRC and Uganda prompted WHO’s 17 May 2026 public health emergency of international concern, with spread to neighboring countries amid conflict and displacement that hinder surveillance and care. articleSummary: On 2026-06-04, Bach Mai Hospital in Vietnam reports a surge of severe tetanus cases treated at the Institute of Tropical Medicine Bach Mai. articleHeadline: Ebola Outbreak Renews Interest in Virus-Catching Blood Filter
articleSummary: As of 2026-06-04, the Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak is centered in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo with limited spillover into Uganda; roughly 1,000 suspected cases and fewer than 300 related deaths. Revived interest centers on the Hemopurifier, an extracorporeal blood-filtering device using snowdrop plant proteins to trap viral particles as blood passes through a dialysis circuit. Aethlon Medical says the system is ready to deploy; FDA compassionate-use authorization for up to 20 patients across 10 U.S. sites has existed since 2014 and remains active. The current outbreak is far smaller than the 2013–2014 West Africa epidemic (~28,000 cases, ~11,000 deaths).

articleSummary: One imported dengue fever case in Kaohsiung, Taiwan: a Vietnamese student, employed in a Sanmin District restaurant, returned from Vietnam and was feverish on June 1 (38.6°C) at Kaohsiung airport. An airport NS1 rapid test was negative, but he was escorted to Minsheng Hospital and placed in isolation. On June 2, a PCR test confirmed dengue fever. The patient did not enter the community or attend school, resulting in no transmission risk. Rapid airport screening and immediate isolation helped avert spread and avoided emergency chemical spraying. Southeast Asia remains dengue-endemic; travelers returning within 14 days should monitor health and seek care for fever, headache, retro-orbital pain, myalgia/arthralgia, or rash, and inform clinicians of TOCC (travel, occupation, contact, cluster history).

articleSummary: Two Brazilians were suspected of Ebola after arriving in Rio from Uganda and in São Paulo after a trip to the DRC. Analyses found malaria in the Rio case and meningococcal meningitis in the São Paulo case, amid Uganda and DRC outbreaks, with the WHO declaring a PHEIC. Ebola is a viral disease identified in 1976, named for the Ebola River near the DRC. Transmission is via direct contact with blood, secretions, organs, or other fluids of infected humans or animals, or contaminated objects; it is not airborne. Early symptoms include fever, weakness, muscle pains, headache, and sore throat, often progressing to vomiting, diarrhea, and abdominal pain; severe cases can involve bleeding and organ failure. Fruit bats are natural reservoirs; transmission from wildlife to humans can lead to human-to-human spread. Historically, most cases are in Central/West Africa, especially DRC, Uganda, Guinea, Liberia, Sierra Leone; isolated cases occur elsewhere due to travel.

articleSummary: Two American researchers have been formally charged for allegedly attempting to smuggle vials containing the inactivated monkeypox virus through Detroit Metropolitan Airport. Vincent Munster, head of the virus environment division at Rocky Mountain Laboratories (RML) in Montana, and his assistant Claude Kuw were detained in Detroit, Michigan, in January after returning from a nine-day field mission that included the Democratic Republic of Congo and a stop in Paris, France. A criminal complaint says one defendant initially denied possessing biological materials, but later tests found hidden vials containing samples of the inactivated monkeypox virus for which no disclosure or transport licenses were obtained. articleSummary: Outbreak of Bundibugyo Ebolavirus in the Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda is one of the largest on record with no sign of slowing. The outbreak, first detected January 16 in Serchhip, has since spread to Aizawl, Kolasib (Lungdai), Lawngtlai, and other parts of the state. Aizawl district is the worst-hit with 1,298 pig deaths, followed by Serchhip with 783. On a single Wednesday, 62 pigs died amid fresh cases in Lungdai, Lawngtlai, and parts of Aizawl. In total, 330 families in Aizawl district and 307 in Serchhip have suffered losses. ASF affects pigs and wild boars and poses no human risk. Surveillance and containment efforts continue across affected areas. By comparison, June 3, 2025 saw 4,629 pig deaths and 1,451 cullings.

articleSummary: Ebola virus Bundibugyo strain is spreading in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and Uganda, with no approved vaccines or treatments. articleSummary: Anthrax (carbunclo) in Brazilian cattle, caused by Clostridium chauvoei, yields near-100% mortality. articleSummary: An Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo continues to escalate, with authorities reporting 363 confirmed cases and 62 deaths since the WHO declared a new outbreak on May 15, 2026. Attacks on trained burial teams heighten transmission risk: in Katana, South Kivu, about 30 km north of Bukavu, residents disrupted a team handling infectious corpses, forcing them to abandon a coffin; a similar assault occurred in Bunia, Ituri Province, where four responders were wounded at a grave site. The incidents underscore growing public distrust toward burial protocols and hinder crucial containment efforts. Burial workers adhere to strict infection-control procedures to prevent spread, but direct contact with contaminated bodies remains a major danger. The violence complicates outbreak control as authorities warn that interference with safe burials and exposure to corpses could accelerate transmission.
notes: 進行中のエボラ流行（2026年5月15日宣言、確認症例363例、死亡62例）。South Kivu州Katana地区とIturi州Bunia地区での埋葬チーム襲撃により、公衆衛生上の危機管理が極度に損なわれている。感染制御の失敗と社会的混乱の両面でリスク評価は最高レベル。

articleSummary: Amid the 17th Ebola outbreak in North Kivu's Beni, Democratic Republic of Congo, barrier measures have been expanded to hotels, restaurants, bar owners, and public transport to curb transmission of Ebola virus disease (Bundibugyo strain). Since the outbreak's emergence, provincial tourism authorities have mandated handwashing on entry, social distancing, and avoidance of crowding in hospitality venues; in public transport, passenger capacity is reduced from six to four per vehicle. Inspectors monitor compliance and sanction violations. Local establishments such as Restau Bar Amis Clients Trinite (Matonge) and Hotel Sheraton (Tamende) report implementation, with handwashing kits, temperature checks, and hydroalcoholic gel at tables. Patrons acknowledge preventive measures, though crowding persists in nightclubs. Officials emphasize community awareness and joint responsibility to stop multiform transmission of EVD.

articleHeadline: Sud-Kivu : plus de 6 400 cas de choléra et 80 décès enregistrés entre janvier et mai 2026
articleSummary: Cholera outbreaks persist in South Kivu, Democratic Republic of the Congo. From January to May 2026, health authorities reported 6,494 suspected cholera cases and 80 deaths (case fatality rate 1.2%). Week 22 saw 193 new cases with no deaths. Of the 80 fatalities, 33 occurred in health facilities and 47 in community settings. Across 34 health zones, 23 have recorded at least one case; 65% of cases are concentrated in five zones: Fizi, Ibanda, Ruzizi, Uvira, and Itombwe. In full-year 2025, South Kivu logged 13,027 cases and 99 deaths; in 2024, 3,668 cases and 29 deaths. In early 2026, the province had already notified 4,607 cases and 67 deaths in the first fourteen weeks across 23 zones. Healthcare supply shortages and insufficient community response threaten interruption of transmission. The resurgence adds to concurrent outbreaks, including Ebola, in South Kivu.
notes: 記事サマリーではDRCの南キブ州でのコレラ流行が主題。ブルンジとフィジーはBluedot APIの発生地域に含まれているが、記事本文ではDRCのみが実際の発生地として記述されているため verified_locations に含めず。エボラとコレラの同時流行、前年比での症例急増（2024年3,668→2025年13,027→2026年上期既に4,607）、医療用品不足による対応困難が懸念事項。

articleHeadline: Commentary | Williams Lambers: Ebola virus shows urgency of humanitarian aid
articleSummary: Bundibugyo Ebola virus outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) prompts urgent humanitarian action as the WHO declares a public health emergency of international concern. The outbreak has killed hundreds with suspected cases exceeding a thousand; the virus has spread to Uganda and could reach more nations. There is no vaccine or proven treatment for Bundibugyo Ebola, and the case fatality is estimated at 30–50%. Health workers report insufficient protective equipment and care resources. UNICEF notes more than 2,000 community health workers are deployed, but additional capacity and funding are urgently needed, especially in hard-to-reach areas. The piece links the Ebola response to widespread hunger in the DRC (about 26.5 million affected) and calls for increased donor funding; the WFP is leading hunger relief. It also highlights famine risks in Sudan, South Sudan and Somalia and urges restoring U.S. humanitarian aid funding.

articleSummary: On Monday in Katana, South Kivu, DR Congo, residents attacked a burial team trained in safe and dignified handling of Ebola victims, forcing them to abandon one coffin unburied and sparking fears of infection. The Health Ministry and a local hospital official told Reuters the incident occurred in Katana, about 30 km north of Bukavu, amid rebels linked to the Congo River Alliance/Movement for 23 March. The team is trained to manage highly infectious remains under strict protocols to prevent transmission; local community members later buried the body, a high-risk practice that could fuel further spread. The episode underscores distrust and resistance hindering outbreak response as authorities seek to control the Bundibugyo Ebola strain. A related incident on the previous Monday in Bunia, Ituri, saw a burial-response team attacked at a cemetery, leaving four people injured as Bundibugyo cases were confirmed there.

articleHeadline: Ebola et environnement : l'arrêt des perturbations écologiques recommandé pour stopper l'émergence du virus - ACP
articleSummary: As of 4 June 2026 in Kinshasa, an expert on protected areas management in the Democratic Republic of the Congo urges an immediate halt to ecological disturbances and the safeguarding of tropical forests as the principal prevention against Ebola virus emergence. Ebola is presented as an environment-health disease that surfaces when the faunal–forest–human balance is disrupted. The virus persists in African tropical forests via a sylvatic cycle linking reservoir species—frugivorous bats, primates, and antelopes—to humans who contact them or their fluids, triggering spillover. Deforestation and intensive agriculture fragment habitats, driving reservoir species toward inhabited areas. Practical measures favor a One Health approach at Kahuzi-Biega National Park (PNKB): enhanced wildlife surveillance, early-warning alerts for unusual mammal deaths, strict control of contact zones, and robust anti-poaching and illegal charcoal efforts. Protecting biodiversity is described as the essential shield for public health.
notes: 記事はエボラウイルスの出現リスク要因（生態系破壊、森林伐採）と予防戦略（One Healthアプローチ）に関する専門家の提言であり、現在のアウトブレイク確認報告ではない。DRCでのエボラ動向に関する情報源として継続監視が推奨される。

articleSummary: Mongbwalu, Democratic Republic of the Congo, as of 4 June 2026, Ebola persists in a remote mining town where distrust that Ebola exists fuels transmission. articleHeadline: Ebola had 'big head-start', WHO chief Tedros warns
articleSummary: As of 2026-06-04, Ebola driven by the Bundibugyo strain has a “big head-start” in central Africa, with WHO chief Tedros warning authorities are still catching up. The outbreak centers on Ituri Province in eastern DR Congo, with spillover into North and South Kivu and neighboring Uganda. The Bundibugyo variant has no approved medicine or vaccine. In DR Congo, 344 confirmed cases and 60 deaths have been reported since mid-May; 166 suspected cases remain (down from 906). A 3-year-old boy suspected to have died from Ebola was buried in Mubende, Uganda, underscoring cross-border concern. Health authorities are rushing to improve testing capacity, isolate contacts, and pursue a cure for the strain. Separately, the US plans a quarantine facility at Kenya’s Laikipia airbase to isolate Americans who visited DR Congo; Kenyan protests persist, with ~20 flights landed and 23 centers planned, no patients yet.

articleHeadline: Risk factor analysis and construction of risk nomogram for severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome based on clinical classification
articleSummary: Severe Fever with Thrombocytopenia Syndrome (SFTS), caused by a novel bunyavirus with high mortality, is analyzed in China using 437 hospitalized patients from the First Affiliated Hospital of USTC and Hefei Second People’s Hospital (Jan 2022–Dec 2024). Patients are categorized as mild (177; 40.5%), severe (202; 46.2%), and critical (58; 13.3%). Multivariate logistic regression identified seven independent risk factors for progression to severe/critical: IL-6 >50 pg/mL (OR 7.82), altered consciousness (OR 6.85), hemorrhagic manifestations (OR 4.21), hs-CRP >10 mg/L (OR 3.45), pulmonary infection (OR 2.94), AST >200 U/L (OR 2.13), and age ≥65 (OR 1.68). A nomogram with internal validation achieved C-index 0.806 and ROC-AUC 0.806, with calibration indicating good fit (Hosmer-Lemeshow P 0.512) and overall sensitivity 78.5% and specificity 81.9%. The seven-factor model facilitates early identification of high-risk SFTS patients, supporting personalized treatment and early intervention strategies.
